subject.title: [Bug]: codex turn watchdogs have inconsistent defer guards and no wall-clock ceiling; attempt-idle aborts long quiet native tool calls

question: Should the Codex app-server wall-clock ceiling be derived from the effective run/terminal timeout budget, or should OpenClaw intentionally impose a fixed absolute Codex turn cap?
rationale: Current main already preserves explicit long-run timeout budgets, while the requested wall-clock ceiling changes runtime liveness semantics and the linked PR has compatibility risk if it uses a fixed cap.

options.title: Require Budget-Derived Ceiling
options.body: Derive the absolute ceiling from the effective run or terminal budget and require tests for default and longer-than-default configured runs before merging the linked PR.

options.title: Accept Fixed Ceiling
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally cap Codex app-server turns at a fixed duration, but that should be documented as an upgrade behavior change and proven with real behavior evidence.

options.title: Split The Policy Work
options.body: Land only the blocker-order and defer-guard repair now and track the wall-clock ceiling as a separate maintainer-owned timeout policy decision.

recommendation.title: Require Budget-Derived Ceiling
recommendation.body: Derive the absolute ceiling from the effective run or terminal budget and require tests for default and longer-than-default configured runs before merging the linked PR.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the adjacent run-budget-aware timeout behavior that the wall-clock policy must preserve or intentionally change.
